title: Watch Out for the Piezo2 Link to Orthostasis: Is There a More Complex Ultrafast Body-Wide Piezo2 System Operational?
content: Several underlying protective mechanisms have been identified, yet orthostatic hypotension, a sudden decrease in systemic blood pressure upon standing can frequently occur, especially with aging. The very initial step leading to a cascade of events preventing orthostatic hypotension, and perhaps responsible for orthostatic hypotension, is still under investigation. Piezo2 in vagal ganglia has been shown to contribute to cardiovascular stability by preventing orthostatic hypotension in a time-locked and fine-tuned way to atrial and ventricular systole. Accordingly, a distinct group of vagal neurons with end-net endings in the heart initiate a blood-volume-dependent reflex in response to decreased filling of the heart to compensate for upright posture and hemorrhage. This robust feedback control contributes to counterbalance the impact of gravity in order to serve cardiovascular stability. The current perspective manuscript is aiming to highlight that this finding is only one side of a more complex system. Accordingly, we should consider an underlying novel ultrafast body-wide Piezo2 system, underpinned by the principally Piezo2-coupled autonomic nervous, proprioceptive, visual and auditory and vestibular systems. The basis of this Piezo2-based synchronizing mechanism was first put forward within the brain and thereafter it was hypothesized that Piezo2 may also initiate such a synchronizing mechanism between the periphery and the brain. However, the current manuscript puts into perspective that not only these above mentioned Piezo2-initiated synchronizing mechanisms play a role in autonomic regulation and orthostatic control, but the Piezo2-initatied vestibulo-brain axis integrated in an ultrafast fashion under allostatic stress, and this Piezo2 system is even impacted by the Piezo2-initiated visual-brain and auditory-brain axes. Therefore, the knockout/ablation of PIEZO2 in vagal ganglia not only critically targets this novel complex body-wide Piezo2 mechanism, impacting the autonomous nervous system and orthostatic control, but it highlights Piezo2’s crucial importance with system-wide relevance by mimicking acquired Piezo2 channelopathy or quasi Piezo2 channelopathy (loss of function).
